editorial:
Imagine growing up in Cleveland with a sibling who is your best friend and your biggest headache. That is exactly what you get here. You follow a brother and sister who are both talented musicians trying to make it big in the rock world. The movie feels like a real slice of life, showing the messy side of family ties and the stress of chasing a dream. It is not just about the music, though. It is about how you deal with your parents and the baggage you carry from childhood while trying to find your own voice in the world.

You will really appreciate the chemistry between the leads; they feel like actual siblings who know exactly how to push each other's buttons. The pacing is steady, and the music is a great throwback to the era. While some parts feel a bit slow, the emotional payoffs make it worth your time. If you are into family dramas with a musical twist, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: At the end, the siblings finally stop fighting and realize that their bond is more important than their egos or their careers. They find a way to work together musically without letting their past trauma tear them apart. Instead of one person winning or losing, they reach a peaceful understanding. The movie wraps up with a feeling of hope, showing that they have finally grown up and learned how to support each other as adults.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about family struggles and the music industry.
